answers.answer: Each player takes twelve ordinary turns (three per season across four seasons). Courtship spaces 4, 8, 12, and 16 are event-only: no ordinary player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.

Host order: rotate service (Quarters to Available, then Expended to Quarters); resolve round event, then applicable monument/Servants’ Hall effects; choose an activity tile; invite the exact required gentry; provide all required service; resolve positive favours before negative favours; optionally buy; then put used servants in Expended Service, played gentry in personal discard, and return the activity tile to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required.

Pass order: servants directly to Available Service; recover all gentry in discard to hand; resolve round event then ongoing effects; choose £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; then advance the marker. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit.

Yes. Screening is fixed at the end of step 2, so the 6.1 reputation then screens the PR6 activity and PR6 guests for the entire activity, even if four Service Help payments lower current reputation to 3.4 later. Each Service Help moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; it cannot take one directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Actions — Reputation, wealth and special actions

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; order within each group is up to you. At minimum reputation you cannot take a negative reputation favour first to avoid the loss; the summary says negative losses stop at 1.1 and positives must precede negatives. A money penalty must be fully payable, using positive activity money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money as needed; if you cannot fund it, you cannot play that guest/tile.
answers.evidence: Hosting an activity; Reputation, wealth and special actions

answers.answer: Borrow Money costs 2 reputation increments and gains £100; repeatable. Service Help costs 3 increments and moves one Quarters servant to Available Service; repeatable. Refresh Market costs 4 increments and fully refreshes the Market; the special action is once per turn. At minimum 1.1 you cannot take a special action. Service Help cannot take a servant straight from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Actions — Reputation, wealth and special actions

answers.answer: Host the Butler’s Room Servant Hiring activity using an available butler or underbutler, with no gentry. Take up to two servants other than underbutlers from Servants for Hire into Expended Service, without a fee. Once upgraded, instead recruit one common footman, valet, or lady’s maid from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service; unique servants cannot be recruited.

A housekeeper may substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With a Brushing Room, a footman may substitute for a valet only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, footman) even if that servant type remains available.

The Butler’s Pantry is the only way to acquire an underbutler: buying it takes one from supply into Expended Service. Normally it moves to Quarters at the next service rotation and Available Service at the second subsequent rotation; passing or a Refresh Service VP card can make it available sooner, and Quarters effects can also help once it is there. Another player cannot recruit it because it is unique, not common.

Pay the Market space price plus the tile’s printed modifier; Reserve base price is £300 plus the modifier. The minimum tile price is £100. You may not acquire a duplicate tile you already own. Reputation does not restrict purchasing, so a tile above your reputation may be bought.

When a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into rightmost spaces. A duplicate draw stacks on its matching Market tile and you draw again; qualifying Reserve tiles go straight to Reserve and you draw again. If multiple spaces are filled, sort only the new tiles by sorting number. Buying one tile from a duplicate stack leaves the space occupied, so it does not trigger refill.

After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; later Service draws go there too, with the same exception. After courtship 2, also move Market PR1 tiles to Reserve, and later PR1 draws go there. A full Market refresh after each of the first three courtships is standard.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve — Open Reserve; Refresh

answers.answer: At every courtship first return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall. For courtships 1–3, score tile VP in the current face-up theme category, including negatives and only the currently face-up hybrid category. Highest gets one VP card and chooses one Fairchild; on a tie each tied player draws a VP card and no Fairchild is awarded. Each player discards one secret objective, with simultaneous discards shuffled together and bottom-decked. After courtships 1–3, pass the first-player marker anticlockwise.

Final courtship scores tile VP across all four revealed themes, counting a repeated category twice and its negative VP too. Highest gets one VP card and a Fairchild; tie is broken by highest reputation level (wheel ignored). If still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards. Discard the final objective, then players may use special actions and VP-card benefits where possible before scoring.
answers.evidence: Courtship and seasonal upkeep — Final courtship

answers.answer: End-game VP categories are improvement tiles (all printed face-up VP), gentry in hand and discard, fulfilled objectives, reputation, servants (2 VP each), wealth (1 VP per £200 rounded down), and retained VP cards. Reputation levels 1–7 score 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28 VP. Highest total wins; ties go to a player with the final Fairchild, then highest reputation level, then shared victory. Wheel position never breaks a tie.

Normally receive five objectives at setup and two at round 6; discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three for scoring. Main Library or a VP card can add retained objectives, without causing an extra discard. Simultaneous discards are shuffled together and put face down on the bottom of the deck. Tile objectives require owning the named tiles, not upgrading them.

A VP card may be used immediately when drawn, later on your own turn (multiple cards allowed), and once after final courtship before scoring. Reveal and discard it for its benefit; used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained unused cards stay hidden and score their printed VP; you cannot get both benefit and VP from one card.

A normal activity tile must flip to its upgrade side after first use; an already-upgraded normal tile stays upgraded. A hybrid starts with its underlined icon up and flips after every use, moving to the newly face-up category. Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite each host once, then upgrade into monuments and cannot host again; monument benefit starts on subsequent turns. For a hybrid, only the face-up category counts at courtship and for objectives.

Monuments pay one reputation in the ongoing-effects step on ordinary hosting turns and passes, but not courtship. Servants’ Hall resolves in step 2 when hosting and step 3 when passing: put one available servant on it to lower one opponent by one reputation and gain one yourself; the servant cannot also serve the activity and goes to Expended Service at turn end. It cannot target someone at minimum reputation.

Heritage Guest Suite uses one casual guest from hand; one footman serves the tile and the guest gets normal service. It doubles all guest favours, including negative ones, then upgrades and remains an activity tile. Queen’s Suite uses one prestige guest from hand, a housekeeper on the tile, and normal guest service; double one chosen favour and resolve others normally, then it becomes a monument. Lionheart Suite draws one prestige guest from the deck to attend, uses a butler on the tile and no personal guest service; doubles nonnegative favours, keeps the guest into discard at cleanup, then becomes a monument. All three have a fixed count of one guest, which cannot be changed.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects — Suite activity

answers.answer: Choose a random first player. Starting to that player’s left and going clockwise, players choose an available base family board. Bonuses: Asquith gets the Dowager Countess; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gains £300; York gets an extra footman in Available Service.

Set reputation to level 1, position 1; use the 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 and Max counters with 1 showing and Max at bottom, not 7/8 counters. Each gets one butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid and footman in Available Service; Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour and Bowling Green with starter/building icon showing; and Lord, Lady, Heir and Young Lady. Asquith also gets Dowager Countess. Only Ponsonby starts with money (£300).

For three players, Servants for Hire gets three valets, three lady’s maids, six footmen, and two underbutlers total. No butlers or housekeepers are stocked. Unused servants are returned to the box and unavailable for the game.

Shuffle starter guests separately from the casual deck and deal two starter guests to each player; shuffle every undealt starter back into the casual deck. Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon and otherwise follow normal casual rules, not a separate type during play.
answers.evidence: Setup; Gentry, screening, dismissal and family

answers.answer: For four players, select one double-sided monument per player plus one: five total. Choose at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze. Tiles that later upgrade into monuments always go in the bag and do not count against the setup selection.

Fill six different eligible Market spaces: PR3 or less (including no PR), excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Set aside ineligible draws and return them to the bag after filling; stack duplicate eligible tiles in the same space. Normal tiles enter with upgrade/rose icon hidden; hybrids with underlined hybrid icon showing. Sort spaces by ascending sorting number from the £300 space. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments are ineligible.

Put Alderley Hall standard side up, round marker at 1, and one reminder token per player above the track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal the first theme face up (open courtship) and keep revealed themes in order. Place base Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild face up on Alderley Hall.
At hosting rotation, the servant in Servants’ Quarters moves to Available Service; the servant in Expended Service moves to Servants’ Quarters. An unused available servant remains available.

No immediate Fair reward if Private Study is not upgraded when the round event resolves. The upgraded Study gives £300 and 2 reputation on Village Fair spaces 3 and 9. The event is resolved before choosing/hosting the activity, so upgrading it by hosting later that turn does not change that event result.

The Draw Objectives event resolves as the round-track event before activity choice on the standard space 6. Each player draws two objectives and keeps both secret with their other objectives. Because passing still resolves the event, passing players receive it too.
answers.evidence: Hosting an activity; Round-track events; Passing

answers.answer: Yes. National Holiday ignores PR on all tiles and guests when hosting, so a low-reputation player may play higher-PR ones. All other requirements remain, including service and exact gentry counts/types.

Yes, during Builders’ Holiday you may buy any number from current Market and/or Reserve within funds, at unchanged prices; complete all purchases before sliding/refilling. Do not refresh between purchases. Market Purchase VP-card benefits follow the same single-unchanged-market and no-refresh-between-purchases rules.
answers.evidence: Round-track events; Builders’ Market and Reserve — Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside while drawing replacements; they cannot reappear in that refresh. Refill all six spaces under normal rules, then return the set-aside tiles to the bag and mix. Reserve tiles are left unchanged.

Each symbol is one increment. Crossing wheel position 5 to 1 raises a level; crossing 1 to 5 lowers a level; each full level spans five increments. Standard range is 1.1 minimum to 7.5 (Max.5); losses beyond minimum are ignored. At Max.5, excess reputation is lost unless spent immediately on special actions; special actions can be used before or during a reputation favour to make space.
answers.evidence: Actions — Reputation, wealth and special actions

answers.answer: Money is public, and players may not give or receive money between them. Never spend more than you have. The supply is unlimited; use proxies if needed.
answers.evidence: Actions — Reputation, wealth and special actions

answers.answer: “Ladies” and “Gentlemen” requirements include female/male family members respectively, but a “casual guest” requirement requires that guest type and excludes family. You must play the exact required number, no extra or fewer. Family has no PR and needs no personal service.
answers.evidence: Hosting an activity — Invite gentry; Reputation screening

answers.answer: An ordinary invite acquired as a favour is drawn from the indicated deck, revealed to everyone, and added to hand. For screening, draw the stated number, choose the number to keep, reveal only kept cards, and add them to hand; put rejected cards unrevealed on the bottom of their guest deck.
answers.evidence: Hosting an activity — Enjoy favours; Gentry, screening, dismissal and family

answers.answer: Dismissal is always optional. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, the current activity, or discard, including a guest drawn earlier in the same favours step. Family cannot be dismissed. Put the guest on the bottom of its matching deck; it is no longer yours, does not return on passing, and does not score for you.

Lord: gain £200. Lady: choose to screen two casual guests and keep one, or optionally dismiss one guest. Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Asquith Dowager: gain both £100 and one reputation. Thus Lady and Heir offer choices; Dowager gives both benefits; Lord has a fixed benefit.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family — Base family card

answers.answer: The admirer bonus applies when a male prestige guest attends, so it applies with Charles Fairchild (male prestige) but not a male casual guest or a female prestige guest. The bonus is two reputation. Young Lady still draws one casual guest in all cases.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family — Base family card; Charles Fairchild is male and prestige

answers.answer: Charles is a male prestige guest, has no PR, requires a valet, and gives three reputation. Elizabeth is a female prestige guest, has no PR, requires a lady’s maid, and gives one prestige guest plus two reputation. They are guests, not family cards, so family dismissal immunity does not apply to them.

Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent’s reputation by one. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and costs you one reputation. A player at 1.1 cannot be targeted by an opponent’s reputation-reducing effect.
The Barn gives one reputation each time you host an Estate activity. It gives none merely for owning an Estate tile or when passing.

The Servants’ Quarters tile lets you use one servant from the Servants’ Quarters area each turn, in addition to Available Service; after use it goes to Expended Service. This is distinct from Service Help, which costs 3 reputation increments to move one servant from Quarters to Available Service, and from ordinary hosting rotation, which moves Quarters servants to Available and Expended servants to Quarters.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring — Servants’ Quarters tile; Reputation special actions

answers.answer: The Private Study front activity uses a butler and two family, with no tile favour. After its first use it upgrades permanently into an ongoing tile; it cannot be hosted repeatedly as an activity to gain Village Fair income. Its upgraded side gives £300 and two reputation on Village Fair rounds without staffing or hosting it.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects — Private Study

answers.answer: Unupgraded Main Library uses a butler and two family and draws one extra objective. Upgraded it uses a butler and three family and draws one VP card. The extra objective increases the number retained for final scoring; it does not trigger an extra courtship discard.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects — Main Library; Objectives and VP cards

answers.answer: The Objective VP card draws two objectives and keeps one; put the other on the bottom of the objective deck. This adds one retained objective for final scoring.

Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants directly to Available Service and they can be used immediately, including servants from Expended Service. Service Help only moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service and costs 3 reputation increments.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards — Refresh Service; Reputation special actions

answers.answer: A Hire Servant VP card takes one servant from Servants for Hire, not an underbutler, into Expended Service. It is not immediately available to provide service.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards — Hire Servant

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Guest may return any gentry, including a family member, from personal discard to hand. If returned before Invite Gentry, you may choose it to attend this activity subject to its normal requirements; returning it alone does not play it.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards — Refresh Guest

answers.answer: The basic-servant objective counts common footmen, valets and lady’s maids only; it excludes butlers, housekeepers and underbutlers. Ordinary servant VP counts every servant type and location at 2 VP each; the ten-servant objective gives 7 VP for at least ten servants total.

The monument objective counts monuments, including upgraded Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite. Category bonuses count monuments and hybrids in the category currently shown; a hybrid counts only its face-up category.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference; Improvements and ongoing effects

answers.answer: Nature Group is 11 VP for Barn, Brushing Room, and any one of English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden, or Garden Maze. Domestic Group is 12 VP for Gabled Conservatory and either Main Library or North Library. Tile objectives require owning the named tiles at game end; they need not have been used or upgraded.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference; Objectives and VP cards

answers.answer: Prestige-guest objective gives 1 VP per prestige guest. The every-three-guests objective counts all nonfamily guests, including a final Fairchild; only complete groups of three score, so an incomplete group scores nothing.

The reputation objective gives 7 VP for maximum level 7; the wealth objective gives 10 VP for at least £1200. Reputation wheel position does not change ordinary reputation VP or break reputation ties; level is used.

Both sides of base West Terrace require one butler and exactly three family cards. Unupgraded it draws one prestige guest. Upgraded it draws one prestige guest and optionally dismisses one to four guests from hand, current activity, or discard to the bottom of their decks. It remains an activity tile, not an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects — West Terrace

answers.answer: There is no hand or personal-discard limit. Gentry in your discard pile remain yours and score normally; passing recovers them to hand.
You may inspect every Reserve tile at any time and buy any one, including a tile under another in a stack; you do not have to buy only the top tile. Every Reserve tile is public.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve — Open Reserve

answers.answer: You may choose to host an activity or pass; there is no requirement to host whenever possible. If you lack required gentry or service for a preferred activity, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity is possible, you must pass.

Yes. On a passing turn you may take the free Market refresh, the paid Refresh Market special action, and multiple Market Refresh VP cards, each for a separate full refresh. Only the paid special-action refresh is limited to once per turn; pass and VP refreshes do not use that allowance.
answers.evidence: Actions — Reputation, wealth and special actions
